brief: The Market Ear frames a rates-vs-equities disconnect: 10-year yield RSI is as stretched as the January 2025 local high, the MOVE-VIX gap has blown out, and tech CDS spreads are back near recent highs, yet NDX is not reacting the way it did to CDS stress in July. Deutsche Bank's Jim Reid attributes this year's yield rise mostly to real yields and growth repricing, not inflation expectations. The Market Ear's own read: stronger growth may let the S&P 500 absorb higher yields at the index level, but Russell 2000 weakness shows rate-sensitive stocks already feeling it; if real yields stay elevated, the gap between calm equities and panicked bonds gets harder to ignore. Separately, Goldman Sachs frames the AI capex debate: hyperscalers need $1.42 trillion of 2028-30 revenue for a 15% ROIC on 2026-27 buildout, but their existing $1.69 trillion backlog covers most of it at ~59% conversion, so GS says it is too early to exit AI winners. GS likes NDX upside via short-dated QQQ call spreads, hedging longs with QQQ puts since hyperscaler credit spreads price more AI stress than equity options do.
